title: Throughput SLA windowing, credit computation, and remediation tiers
creator: Emily Chen
description: Define precise measurement windows, burst credit accounting, and a tiered remediation matrix for Dedicated throughput SLAs. Deliver contract language snippets for Sales/Legal and implementation specs for the runtime team.
background: Existing draft SLAs and error-budget language have high-level throughput guarantees but lack deterministic handling for short-term bursts, multi-window smoothing, and a transparent credit calculation customers can audit. This gap causes disputes during incidents and slows Dedicated contract approvals.
goals: Specify rolling and fixed windows used to compute throughput SLA compliance
Design a verifiable credit calculation for missed throughput that is simple to audit
Define remediation tiers tied to severity and recurrence (credits, capacity remediation, contract remedies)
Produce contract-ready clauses and runtime telemetry requirements
scope: Measurement models: fixed-window, rolling-window, and hybrid smoothing
Remediation tier definitions and escalation flows
out_of_scope: Legal approval language finalization (Legal will review the resulting clauses)
acceptance_criteria: PM/Legal prototype clause reviewed and accepted by Sales leadership
Runtime team has an implementation doc with measurable metrics and a test harness
Billing team can compute and apply credits automatically from the telemetry pipeline
A dashboard widget surfaces SLA compliance, window breakdowns, and past credits
measurement_spec: Primary metric: sustained tokens/sec fulfilled at the customer’s allocated capacity over the measurement interval. Measurement windows: 1) Primary rolling window = 24h with 1h slide; 2) Short-term burst window = 5m fixed sample for burst detection; 3) Monthly compliance window = calendar month aggregation. For compliance, a violation occurs if the 24h rolling availability of guaranteed throughput falls below the contracted threshold for more than 3 non-overlapping 1h slices in a 24h period. Short-term bursts reduce the available credit bucket but do not immediately trigger remediation unless they cause sustained 24h deficits.
credit_formula: Credit (USD) = max(0, (ContractedThroughput - ActualFulfilledThroughput) / ContractedThroughput) * ContractMonthlyFee * AdjustmentFactor. AdjustmentFactor = min(1.0, (HoursAffected / 24) * SeverityMultiplier). Example: Customer contracted 100K tokens/hr; actual fulfilled averaged 80K tokens/hr for a 6-hour window causing effective delta = 20%. Monthly fee $20K. Basic credit = 0.20 * 20000 = $4,000. If HoursAffected=6 and SeverityMultiplier=1.0, AdjustmentFactor=0.25, applied credit = $1,000. Credits are capped at 50% of monthly fee per calendar month. All calculations use the 24h rolling window; short-term burst penalties are applied against a rolling credit bucket before monetary credits are issued. Customers can request raw telemetry for audit (see links).
remediation_matrix: Tier 1 (minor, single event): Notify customer, apply computed credit (<=2% monthly fee) automatically, create post-incident report. No SLA escalation.

Tier 2 (repeated within 30 days or moderate severity): Automated capacity surge (if configured), apply computed credit (2-20%), schedule on-call postmortem, offer short-term throughput uplift at partner rates during remediation window.

Tier 3 (severe or sustained deficits across multiple 24h windows): Reserved capacity reconfiguration, priority engineering remediation, apply larger credit (20-50%, capped), right-to-terminate clause becomes available after three consecutive monthly failures (subject to legal review).
telemetry_and_dashboard_requirements: Per-customer tokens/sec timeseries with 1m granularity retained for 90 days
Computed rolling-window compliance signal (24h) and short-term burst counter (5m samples)
Audit export endpoint to pull raw samples for a given contract period
A customer-visible widget showing current credit balance, historical credits, and last incident report
rollout_plan: Week 1: Review measurement definitions with Runtime, Billing, and Legal; finalize telemetry fields
Week 2-3: Runtime implements compliance signal and exposes audit endpoint; Billing prototypes credit calculation job
Week 4: Ship dashboard widget behind feature flag; run closed beta with two pilot Dedicated customers
Week 5: Iterate on formula and documentation based on pilot feedback; Legal drafts contract clauses
Week 6: GA release of SLA clause and automated crediting for new Dedicated contracts
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting. Agreed on 24h rolling primary window and 5m burst samples. Action: ENG to prototype metric.
2026-02-28: Runtime prototype pushed; sampling cadence and retention flagged as potential cost pressure. Billing asked for a capped credit model to limit exposure.
2026-03-05: PM & Legal workshop. Legal prefers explicit monthly cap and right-to-terminate conditions. Suggested contract language drafted and attached.
2026-03-09: Pilot customers identified (Acme AI, Novi Health). CS to schedule instrumented beta starting 2026-03-16.
2026-03-10: Internal review: scaled-down formula approved; moved ‘SeverityMultiplier’ to allow operational override during major incidents. Document submitted for design review (dashboard UX).
decision_log: 2026-02-22: Chosen hybrid measurement model (24h rolling + 5m burst checks) to balance burst tolerance and predictable monthly accounting.
2026-02-28: Adopted capped credit approach (max 50% monthly fee) to bound financial risk.
2026-03-05: Legal requirement: express ‘right-to-terminate’ only after three consecutive monthly breaches; include remediation-first language to encourage fix-first behavior.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: more granular windows give more precise customer experience but increase telemetry cost and noise — hybrid model is a pragmatic compromise.
Potential future: add per-route weighting for customers who spread load unevenly across models (post-GA).
Billing automation should be idempotent; any retroactive changes must be logged and reversible.
